English: Stone Platform
A rough, raised stone platform, hastily assembled by the clan as a site for basic rituals and gatherings, marking the first step in sacred construction.
Walled Stand
A low-walled enclosure built around the stone platform, providing privacy and sanctity for clan rites and shielding from the harsh steppe winds.
Circular Pavilion
A circular wooden pavilion, roofed and adorned with sacred symbols, serving as a formal gathering point for religious leaders and clan elders.
Raised Chamber
A sturdy, elevated chamber built of stone and timber, reserved for sacred relics and the most important of clan ceremonies.
Priests Room
A private chamber richly decorated for the use of the clans head priest, allowing for meditation, study, and the preparation of sacred rites.
Blessed Hall
A grand hall where the clan gathers for the most significant festivals and rituals, its walls adorned with Zoroastrian iconography and banners.
Sanctified Room
A meticulously cleansed and maintained space, set apart for the most sacred fires and purification rites, attended only by the most devout.
Holy Tower
A tall stone tower rising above the camp, visible for miles, serving both as a beacon of faith and as a refuge for sacred texts and relics.
Sanctuary Pavilion
A fortified pavilion dedicated solely to sanctuary and prayer, reserved for the highest clergy and most revered guests.
Zoroastrian Tower of Silence
A monumental stone edifice, where the dead are laid to rest according to ancient Zoroastrian custom. Its presence is a sign of the clans enduring faith and unity.
